how the sexualized appearance of female characters and their gaze in an immersive environment affect attitudes toward women and rape myths.

the results suggest that virtual females who conform to gender-stereotypical appearance and behaviors may be more influential than those who do not.
the virtual world can have a significant influence on the attitudes of the user.

this study found that men and women who were exposed to a highly stereotypical virtual female character (suggestively clad and high eye gaze, or conservatively clad and low eye gaze) demonstrated more sexism and more rape myth acceptance than did men and women exposed to a nonstereotypical virtual female character.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
virtual characters that conform to gender-stereotypical expectations are likely to be judged more harshly than those that violate expectations.
we found no evidence of a “virtual reality effect,” whereby participants’ behavior in the virtual world was different from their behavior in the physical world.
the effects of virtual reality are not just limited to the virtual space but also have an impact on the real world.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the virtual environment is a powerful medium for the study of gender stereotypes and sexualized appearance.
the way female characters are portrayed in virtual worlds matters.
the effects of virtual characters’ appearance on gender stereotyping may not be limited to the virtual world but may spill over into real world behavior.
